meta.subject: Fractions
meta.curriculum_context: Ghanaian upper primary (B.S. 4-6), generated against a 10-node skill graph.
meta.q_vector_convention: A 10-bit list aligned with node_order. A 1 indicates the skill is cognitively required to perform the procedure correctly. Minimum-cognitive convention: only skills strictly needed are marked, not all DAG ancestors. Under KST with a correct surmise relation, the lattice handles ancestor credit automatically. If you switch to strict DINA, expand each q_vector to include all DAG ancestors of the marked skills.
design_notes: Items deliberately avoid relying on addition or subtraction of fractions since those nodes are absent from the user's DAG. A production version should add 'Add/subtract fractions' and 'Common denominator' nodes before generating PEDMAS items that mix +/- with x/÷.
All items are multiple-choice for paper administration and machine-checkable scoring. Distractors are aligned to named misconceptions from the misconceptions section where possible.
Currency uses Ghana Cedis (GH₵). Names and contexts use Ghanaian referents (Kofi, Ama, Akua, Kwame, Yaa, Esi; kelewele, jollof, plantain, watermelon, market settings).
Vulgar-fraction unicode characters (½, ⅓, ⅔, ¼, ¾, ⅕, ⅖, ⅗, ⅘) are used for mixed numbers; slash notation (a/b) for general fractions.
Each item has a distractor_rationales field giving the misconception each wrong option targets, useful both for review and for downstream misconception-level diagnosis beyond skill mastery.

Multiplication.label: confuses_with_addition
Multiplication.description: Computes a sum instead of a product (e.g. 6 × 7 = 13).

Multiplication.label: drops_zero_in_tens
Multiplication.description: Multiplies the non-zero digits but forgets to attach the trailing zero when multiplying by tens (e.g. 28 × 30 = 84 instead of 840).

Multiplication.label: ignores_place_value
Multiplication.description: Multiplies digit-by-digit without preserving place value (e.g. 23 × 12 → 2×1 + 3×2 = 8).

Multiplication.label: tables_breakdown_above_seven
Multiplication.description: Confident on 2-5 tables but breaks down at 6-9 (e.g. 7 × 8 produced as 54 or 64).

Division.label: swaps_dividend_and_divisor
Division.description: Computes divisor ÷ dividend (e.g. for 12 ÷ 4 the student computes 4 ÷ 12).

Division.label: drops_remainder
Division.description: Reports only the quotient when a remainder exists (e.g. 17 ÷ 4 = 4).

Division.label: smaller_cannot_be_divided
Division.description: Believes a smaller number cannot be divided by a larger one (e.g. 3 ÷ 6 = 0 or 'undefined').

Division.label: division_always_shrinks
Division.description: Believes the quotient must be smaller than the dividend (so 6 ÷ ½ should be < 6).

Division.label: misaligns_place_value_long_div
Division.description: Brings down digits to the wrong column in long division, producing answers off by a factor of ten.

Concept_of_fraction.label: treats_as_two_whole_numbers
Concept_of_fraction.description: Reads 1/2 as two separate numbers rather than as a single quantity.

Concept_of_fraction.label: ignores_equal_parts_requirement
Concept_of_fraction.description: Counts any partition as a valid fraction even when the parts are unequal.

Concept_of_fraction.label: shaded_over_unshaded
Concept_of_fraction.description: Writes the fraction as shaded:unshaded rather than shaded:total (e.g. 3 of 5 shaded read as 3/2).

Concept_of_fraction.label: fraction_only_means_division
Concept_of_fraction.description: Recognises 1/2 as '1 divided by 2' = 0.5 but cannot identify 1/2 of a shape, or vice versa.

Equivalent_fractions.label: adds_same_number_to_top_and_bottom
Equivalent_fractions.description: Believes 1/2 = 2/3 because 1 became 2 and 2 became 3 (added 1 to each).

Equivalent_fractions.label: multiplies_only_one_part
Equivalent_fractions.description: Multiplies the numerator (or only the denominator) by a factor (e.g. 1/2 = 2/2).

Equivalent_fractions.label: thinks_visual_size_matters
Equivalent_fractions.description: Believes equivalence depends on the size of the diagram drawn.

Equivalent_fractions.label: different_numbers_means_different_fraction
Equivalent_fractions.description: Cannot accept that 1/3 and 2/6 are the same value because the digits differ.

Equivalent_fractions.label: scales_top_and_bottom_by_different_factors
Equivalent_fractions.description: Multiplies the top and bottom by different numbers (e.g. 1/2 = 2/6, top × 2, bottom × 3).

Simplifying_fractions.label: reduces_only_numerator
Simplifying_fractions.description: Divides only the top of the fraction (e.g. 8/12 → 1/12).

Simplifying_fractions.label: stops_at_first_common_factor
Simplifying_fractions.description: Divides by a small common factor and stops, even when further reduction is possible (e.g. 24/36 → 12/18, leaves as final).

Simplifying_fractions.label: subtracts_instead_of_divides
Simplifying_fractions.description: Subtracts a common number from top and bottom (e.g. 24/36 → 22/34).

Simplifying_fractions.label: thinks_simplifying_changes_value
Simplifying_fractions.description: Believes 6/9 and 2/3 are different fractions with different values.

Mixed_to_improper.label: writes_whole_as_numerator
Mixed_to_improper.description: Converts 2⅓ to 2/3, ignoring the existing fractional part.

Mixed_to_improper.label: forgets_to_add_numerator
Mixed_to_improper.description: Multiplies whole × denominator but stops without adding the existing numerator (e.g. 2⅓ → 6/3).

Mixed_to_improper.label: changes_the_denominator
Mixed_to_improper.description: Alters the denominator during the conversion.

Improper_to_mixed.label: swaps_quotient_and_remainder
Improper_to_mixed.description: Places the remainder where the whole-number quotient should go and vice versa (e.g. 11/4 → 3¼ instead of 2¾).

Improper_to_mixed.label: drops_remainder
Improper_to_mixed.description: Reports only the whole-number quotient with the fraction missing (e.g. 11/4 → 2).

Improper_to_mixed.label: uses_quotient_as_denominator
Improper_to_mixed.description: Uses the quotient as the denominator in the fractional part.

Improper_to_mixed.label: no_conversion_done
Improper_to_mixed.description: Leaves the improper fraction unchanged, assuming it is already in the requested form.

Improper_to_mixed.label: denominator_changes
Improper_to_mixed.description: Modifies the denominator instead of keeping it constant through the conversion.

Multiplying_fractions.label: finds_common_denominator_first
Multiplying_fractions.description: Treats multiplication like addition: rewrites with a common denominator before multiplying.

Multiplying_fractions.label: multiplies_only_numerators
Multiplying_fractions.description: Multiplies the numerators but keeps one of the original denominators (e.g. 2/3 × 4/5 = 8/3).

Multiplying_fractions.label: expects_product_to_be_larger
Multiplying_fractions.description: Rejects answers smaller than both factors because the student believes the product must exceed both.

Dividing_fractions.label: forgets_to_invert
Dividing_fractions.description: Just multiplies the two fractions as written (e.g. 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/8).

Dividing_fractions.label: inverts_wrong_fraction
Dividing_fractions.description: Inverts the dividend instead of the divisor (e.g. 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 4/3 × 1/2 = 4/6).

Dividing_fractions.label: divides_top_and_bottom_directly
Dividing_fractions.description: Divides numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator (e.g. 6/8 ÷ 2/4 = 3/2).

Dividing_fractions.label: expects_quotient_to_be_smaller
Dividing_fractions.description: Believes division must yield a smaller result, so rejects quotients > 1 when dividing by a fraction < 1.

PEDMAS.label: works_left_to_right
PEDMAS.description: Computes the expression in written order regardless of precedence (e.g. 1/2 × 2/3 ÷ 1/4 treated as ((1/2 × 2/3) × 1/4) when ÷ is mishandled).

PEDMAS.label: separates_multiplication_from_division
PEDMAS.description: Believes all × must happen before all ÷ (or vice versa), instead of left-to-right within the same precedence tier.

PEDMAS.label: ignores_brackets
PEDMAS.description: Computes through brackets as if they were not present.

PEDMAS.label: treats_division_as_multiplication
PEDMAS.description: Converts ÷ to × without performing the inversion step, conflating the two operations under PEDMAS.

PEDMAS.label: drops_operation_during_chaining
PEDMAS.description: When chaining three or more operations, forgets or skips one (e.g. 1/2 × 2/3 ÷ 1/4 → student stops at 1/2 × 2/3).

distractor_rationales.40: off-by-two slip on the 6 times table

single_skill_items.rationale: Basic multiplication fact. The key distractor (13) screens for students still adding when asked to multiply.

single_skill_items.stem: Kofi has 15 baskets of mangoes. Each basket holds 30 mangoes. How many mangoes does he have in total?

distractor_rationales.150: drops_zero_in_tens (computes 15 × 3 = 45 then attaches one zero incorrectly, or 15 × 30 read as 15 × 10)
distractor_rationales.4500: drops_zero_in_tens in the other direction (attaches an extra zero)

single_skill_items.rationale: Two-digit by two-digit multiplication with a trailing zero. Distractors target the most common place-value errors.

single_skill_items.stem: Ama wants to share 17 oranges equally among 4 friends. How many oranges does each friend get, and how many are left over?

distractor_rationales.3 each, 5 left over: computes 17 ÷ 5 instead of 17 ÷ 4, or other off-by-one error
distractor_rationales.4 each, 0 left over: drops_remainder (reports just the quotient, ignores leftover)

single_skill_items.rationale: Whole-number division with explicit remainder, framed as a sharing word problem.
Tests whether students accept dividing a smaller whole number by a larger one. Common misconception even at upper primary.

single_skill_items.stem: A rectangle is divided into 5 equal parts. 2 of those parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
single_skill_items.rationale: Foundational part-whole identification. Distractor 2/3 is the specific shaded:unshaded misconception.

single_skill_items.stem: Two friends each cut a kelewele plate. Kofi cuts his into 4 equal pieces and shades 1. Ama cuts hers into 4 pieces of different sizes and shades 1. Whose shaded part is exactly 1/4 of the whole?

distractor_rationales.Neither: over-rejection, possibly does not recognise Kofi's case either

single_skill_items.rationale: Probes the equal-parts axiom directly. Distractor 'Both' is the canonical misconception.
Tests recognition of equivalence by integer scaling. Each distractor maps to a named procedural misconception.

distractor_rationales.10: scales_top_and_bottom_by_different_factors (multiplies bottom by 3 but top by some other amount)

single_skill_items.rationale: Requires recognising the multiplicative scale factor between the two denominators (×3) and applying it to the numerator.

distractor_rationales.1/3: reduces_only_numerator (divides 6 by 3 but leaves 9, then writes 2/9 → simplified to 1/3 by further error) or random simplification
distractor_rationales.3/4: subtracts_instead_of_divides (6-3 over 9-5) or other arithmetic error

single_skill_items.rationale: Single-step simplification by the GCD (3). 6/9 was chosen because the GCD is the only common factor, so partial reduction is impossible without arriving at the answer.

distractor_rationales.1/2: incorrect partial reduction or wrong factor

single_skill_items.rationale: Multi-step simplification (GCD = 6). Distractors 4/6 and 6/9 both probe the 'stops at first common factor' misconception by representing each of the two intermediate states.
Classic mixed-to-improper conversion. Each distractor captures a distinct named procedural error.

single_skill_items.stem: Ama bought 3¾ kg of yam at the market. Express this as an improper fraction in kg.

distractor_rationales.7/4: adds_whole_and_numerator (3 + 3 = 6 ... but writes 3+4 = 7), or other adds-and-confuses error
distractor_rationales.13/4: miscount of the multiplication (3 × 4 = 12, then +1 instead of +3)

single_skill_items.rationale: Conversion in a word-problem context. The denominator 4 stresses students who memorised the procedure only for thirds.

distractor_rationales.2¼: uses_quotient_as_denominator or remainder confusion (correct quotient 2, but writes 1 instead of 3 for remainder)

single_skill_items.rationale: Improper-to-mixed conversion. Distractor 3¼ is the canonical quotient/remainder swap.

single_skill_items.stem: Akua walked 17/5 km from her home to the market. Write this distance as a mixed number.

distractor_rationales.2⅖: drops the quotient by one (17 ÷ 5 mistaken as 12 ÷ 5)
distractor_rationales.3⅗: swaps_quotient_and_remainder (writes remainder 3 instead of 2 over the denominator)

single_skill_items.rationale: Conversion with denominator 5 (less rehearsed than 4). Word-problem framing tests transfer.

distractor_rationales.8/8: multiplies tops correctly but adds bottoms or similar mixed error

single_skill_items.rationale: Direct fraction multiplication. Distractors map cleanly onto the three classic procedural errors.

single_skill_items.stem: Yaa has 3/4 kg of rice. She uses 2/5 of it to cook jollof. How much rice did she use, in kg?

distractor_rationales.5/4: treats 'of' as 'plus' or other addition error

single_skill_items.rationale: Word-problem framing for fraction multiplication. The correct answer is intentionally not in lowest terms (3/10) to keep this a pure multiplication item; an alternative version requiring simplification appears as MULTI_003.

distractor_rationales.1/2: divides_top_and_bottom_directly (3÷1 over 4÷2 = 3/2, then mis-simplifies; or other slip)

single_skill_items.rationale: Canonical invert-and-multiply item. Distractors cover the three highest-frequency procedural failures named in the misconceptions list.

single_skill_items.stem: Kwame has 6/8 of a tray of meat pies. He divides his portion into pieces, each one 1/4 of a full tray. How many pieces does he get?
single_skill_items.rationale: Sharing word problem requiring fraction division. The whole-number quotient encourages students to check their answer for plausibility (expects_quotient_to_be_smaller misconception is implicitly probed).

distractor_rationales.1/3: completed only the first step (1/2 × 2/3 = 1/3) and stopped — drops_operation_during_chaining
distractor_rationales.3/4: miscounts somewhere or selects a familiar-looking fraction

single_skill_items.rationale: Three-operation chain with left-to-right ÷ and ×. The dominant misconceptions both produce specific named distractors.
Tests bracket-respect plus invert-and-multiply. Distractor 1/4 is the dominant 'treats ÷ as ×' error.

distractor_rationales.2/3: ignores the whole part (multiplies only the fractional part by 2/3)
distractor_rationales.5/7: adds_numerators_and_denominators across an incorrectly converted mixed number
distractor_rationales.21/12: conversion or multiplication slip (computes 7×3 / 4×3 retaining the conversion factor)

multi_skill_items.rationale: Requires converting 1¾ to 7/4 and then multiplying. Tests whether the student can chain two procedures cleanly; the dominant failure is to skip the conversion step.

multi_skill_items.stem: Esi wrote 12/18 on her exercise book. Express this as a fraction with denominator 3.

distractor_rationales.4/3: stops_at_first_common_factor (divides by 3 only, gets 4/6, then misrepresents)

multi_skill_items.rationale: Combines simplification with the equivalence concept — the student must recognise that simplifying 12/18 to lowest terms produces the requested denominator. Probes both nodes simultaneously.

multi_skill_items.stem: Compute 4/6 × 3/8 and give your answer in lowest terms.

distractor_rationales.1/3: simplification mismatch (divides by wrong common factor or stops early)
distractor_rationales.12/48: correct multiplication but did not simplify

multi_skill_items.rationale: Multiplies first, then simplifies. The distractor 12/48 specifically probes students who got the multiplication right but stopped before simplifying — useful for separating those two skills in the diagnostic.

Heaviest multi-skill item. Requires converting 1½, applying PEDMAS order, multiplying, then dividing by inversion. Misclassification here points to which of the four sub-skills failed; the distractor profile is informative.

multi_skill_items.stem: Compute 1½ × 2½ and write the answer as a mixed number.

distractor_rationales.2½: multiplies whole parts only (1×2 = 2) and arbitrarily places the half
distractor_rationales.5/4: ignores one of the mixed numbers entirely
distractor_rationales.15/4: correct multiplication but did not convert back to mixed number form

multi_skill_items.rationale: Round-trip through both conversion nodes plus multiplication. Distractor 15/4 specifically separates students who can do the multiplication but cannot convert back.

distractor_rationales.1/3: computed 5/2 ÷ 5/4 = 2 then misapplied the next step, or other compounded error

multi_skill_items.rationale: Mirror of MULTI_004 with division coming first. Probes whether the student handles left-to-right precedence within the ×/÷ tier correctly, alongside the two conversion-then-operate sub-procedures.
